states.empty: Batch is the default; the sample is explicitly labeled public/example and is calculated only after processing.
states.fileSelected: Graphite dashed-border filename surface; mapping preview and process control. Reads/configuration blocked while busy.
states.processing: Counts, native progress, pause/resume/cancel and pending rows remain visible. Cancellation preserves working rows.
states.selection: Active row uses selected surface; reference cell, numbered selected marker and inspector reference use cyan. Click/keyboard row selection and marker selection share row state.
states.review: Manual positions remain review-required; score denotes evidence and manual score is a dash. Closed source disclosure still exposes unavailable/empty counts.
states.filtering: Filter/search can show no matches. Table pages at 100 rows; exported selection retains the entire selected lot. Next review reconciles active reference and moves keyboard focus.
states.export: CSV/XLSX/GeoJSON/Shapefile. Completion by ledger heading. Starting export clears old completion; failures remain outside mobile entry disclosure and preserve selection.
states.individualQuery: Secondary mode with labelled address/comuna inputs; same map, evidence and shared results.
states.legacyComparison: ?design=classic retains the shared file/rows/corrections and earlier Swiss view. Its palette and fonts are excluded from this default system.

map.geometry: Coordinates and complete result street polyline unchanged by presentation. fitBounds uses animate:false; no decorative camera travel.
map.candidateStyle: Actual native candidate circle markers preserve black border/white fill (radius6,weight2); candidates are not cyan-selected evidence.
map.editing: Crosshair cursor; map click or selected-marker drag writes manual coordinates with review semantics.

extraction.primitiveAuthority: DESIGN.md frontmatter; no second primitive-token array in this sidecar.
extraction.snippets: Literal scoped default-workshop values are used because the existing root survey variables belong to the legacy classic view. All preview classes are prefixed ds-. Components need no React or icon runtime.
extraction.excluded: Legacy classic tokens/type, surface mode, speculative future components, provider readiness and accuracy claims.

evidence.checks: Recorded browser checks all pass, including 1440/1304/1024/768/390/320 widths, pointer/reduced motion, exports/manual state, mobile failure recovery and 103-row pagination/cancellation. Lint/build passed in the parent workflow.
evidence.limits: Remote sources mocked unavailable/empty; local IDE and map tiles real. Browser reflow was equivalent to zoom, not a real browser-zoom study. Supabase ingestion/Auth/Edge deployment remain pending.
evidence.assets: No generated shipping raster. Native geometry and real runtime OSM tiles; font OFL license retained.
evidence.notCanonized: No unresolved material design defect after the scoped verdict. Inherited catalog size/large-lot marker limits and legacy CSS do not become system rules.

narrative.overview:
Azimut's current functional proposal is a cartographic workshop: geometric lettering, graphite working surfaces and a repeated azimuth bearing give a GIS tool an expressive identity. The lowercase wordmark and local Outfit face answer the user's rejection of the former typography and anonymous identity. This document records the implemented proposal; aesthetic acceptance by the user remains open.

Art comes from native vector geometry and restrained response to input. Working content retains ordinary buttons, inputs, tables, disclosures and a real map. Bright colors identify actions, selection, review and provenance; the bearing is a brand gesture and conveys no geographic evidence. The earlier Swiss comparison remains available as a legacy view and is outside this default system.
keyCharacteristics: Locally served Outfit with tabular figures and a lowercase wordmark.
Graphite layers with distinct action, selection, review and provenance colors.
One repeated native azimuth symbol and finite, optional motion.
Real cartographic geometry, visible evidence and standard web controls.

rules.name: Linked Reference
rules.body: Use cyan to connect the selected row reference, map number and evidence reference. Keep the same row identity visible in all three.

rules.name: Evidence Before Certainty
rules.body: Keep status words, method and source visible beside their colors. An evidence score must never become a probability or a metric-precision claim.

rules.name: One Typeface
rules.body: Use Outfit for display, controls, data and captions. Distinguish roles with size, weight and spacing; retain tabular numerals for coordinates and row references.

rules.name: Tonal Frames
rules.body: Separate working regions with graphite tones and a fine slate boundary. Reserve the observed diffuse shadow for floating map controls.

rules.name: Steady Alternative
rules.body: Reduced motion keeps the bearing, selected marker and street geometry visible while disabling decorative pointer rotation, drawing and transitions.

dos: Do use the existing accent roles and keep status text beside color.
Do reuse the same row reference across table, marker and evidence.
Do retain the locally served Outfit face, its OFL license and tabular figures.
Do expose keyboard focus with the observed cyan outline and lime header outline.
Do keep map attribution visible and restore unfiltered tiles in the light map view.
Do keep manual locations marked for review and source failures visible.
donts: Don't present this recorded proposal as a user-approved visual identity.
Don't add a second import action to the current batch entry state.
Don't make branded bearing motion imply geographic direction or precision.
Don't add decorative animation loops or restore pointer rotation under reduced motion.
Don't replace actual map geometry with decorative cartographic imagery.
Don't merge the legacy Swiss typography or palette into this default identity.
